thread:
sophie (support): ACME reported a sharp p99 regression on completions (ticket #34567). They hit lots of 429s and several client-side timeouts around 09:02 UTC. Repro steps from them below.
chloe (customer-success): they said it started when their nightly report job kicked off (~09:00 UTC). tenant: acme-prod. Customer says this only happens a few times a week but it's blocking their SLA.
oliver (eng-oncall): pinging eng-runtime + eng-sre. any quick signals? priority: customer-facing, high.
maria (eng-runtime): looking at metrics for tenant=acme-prod. admission queue spiked on dedicated pool dp-eu-central-2 at 08:59:30 -> avg queue length ~1k, p99 queue wait ~1.8s. model workers saturated (GPU util 96-99%). KV cache hit rate unchanged. Looks like a request pileup + tight tenant concurrency cap.
monitoring-bot: alert: admissions.queue_length > 800 (dp-eu-central-2) at 08:59:58; p99_request_wait=1.78s; p95_latency=820ms; p99_latency=3.6s
kevin (eng-sre): autoscaler healthy? any pods OOM/evicted? I see a burst of queued tasks and a slow scale-up because the scale policy is minReplicaGrowth=15m for that pool. That explains the lag. Also noticed several pre-warmed replicas were marked "draining" due to a stale drain-label bug.
oliver (eng-oncall): customer repro steps (from ticket):
```
# single-line repro
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <ACME_TOKEN>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-large","prompt":"[big-batch]...","max_tokens":512}'
# they do ~200 concurrent of these during nightly job
```
sophie (support): attaching sample headers and request IDs from their logs: req=ry8743, ry8744, ry8750 (all 429/timeout). Customer also included the job manifest showing concurrency=200.
maria (eng-runtime): short-term plan: 1) temporarily raise tenant concurrency cap (acme-prod) from 20 -> 80; 2) reroute traffic for acme-prod to spare burst pool dp-burst-1; 3) enable fail-fast shed policy for long-running bulk jobs to avoid head-of-line blocking; 4) file follow-up to reduce minReplicaGrowth and fix drain-label bug.
kevin (eng-sre): agree. i'll also disable draining on pre-warm group so we don't lose capacity during scale events.
oliver (eng-oncall): executing increase + reroute now.
oliver (eng-oncall): run: 
```
# bump concurrency cap
curl -s -X POST https://control-plane.internal/tenants/acme-prod/limits \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"concurrency":80}'
# add routing tag
curl -s -X POST https://control-plane.internal/routing/tenants/acme-prod \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"prefer_pools":["dp-burst-1"]}'
```
deploy-bot: routing-update: tenant acme-prod -> dp-burst-1 (started) | change_id=chg-202603170900
deploy-bot: concurrency-update: tenant acme-prod concurrency=80 | change_id=chg-202603170901
maria (eng-runtime): watching queue metrics... queue length starting to drain. pre-scaled burst pool added 12 replicas; GPU util on dp-eu-central-2 dropping.
monitoring-bot: info: dp-eu-central-2: queue_length 1100 -> 420 (09:04:12); dp-burst-1: queue_length 0 -> 320 (09:04:30)
maria (eng-runtime): p95 latency now ~340ms, p99 ~630ms for acme-prod. still slightly above baseline but much better. KV cache warmup is ongoing.
oliver (eng-oncall): rolling restart on the draining pre-warm nodes to clear stuck queues: `kubectl rollout restart ds/worker-prewarm -n inference-eu` (oncall did)
kevin (eng-sre): changed scaler policy ticket filed: INF-7893 (minReplicaGrowth -> 2m for burst pools). Will follow up.
chloe (customer-success): I messaged ACME. they confirmed latency is back down and 429s stopped. they want RCA + permanent mitigation.
sophie (support): thanks team. Customer requested: 1) short RCA, 2) any rate-limit guidance for their nightly job (preferred per-minute rate), 3) timeline for permanent fix.
maria (eng-runtime): RCA draft: spike in ACME's scheduled batch (200 concurrent requests) exceeded tenant concurrency cap and hit dedicated pool dp-eu-central-2. Autoscaler didn't grow fast enough due to minReplicaGrowth and pre-warm nodes were draining due to a label bug, causing admission queue buildup and p99 regressions. Immediate mitigation was to increase tenant concurrency and route to burst pool; longer-term mitigations: adjust autoscaler policy, fix drain-label bug, implement tenant-local surge detection + automatic short-term burst routing.
kevin (eng-sre): follow-up tasks: INF-7893 (autoscaler policy), INF-7901 (drain-label hotfix), INF-7902 (tenant surge detector + automatic reroute). propose default tenant concurrency to 50 for paid dedicated customers and documentation for customers to limit bulk concurrent jobs.
chloe (customer-success): ACME asked for suggested throttling for their job. recommendation: keep concurrency <= 50 and spread over 5 minutes, or use our bulk-upload endpoint which supports async jobs and backoff.
sophie (support): I'll send the RCA + recommended throttling to ACME and propose a short follow-up call.
maria (eng-runtime): quick note: include the temporary mitigation IDs in RCA (chg-202603170900, chg-202603170901) and metric snapshots.
oliver (eng-oncall): closing immediate incident; marking thread resolved. :white_check_mark:
chloe (customer-success): ACME confirmed via DM: "confirmed, performance normal, will throttle nightly runs." :thumbsup:
kevin (eng-sre): leaving this here for postmortem owners. assigning to eng-runtime for root-cause and eng-sre for infra changes.
sophie (support): thanks all. I'll update ticket #34567 and attach this thread.
